// `Map<K, V>` is a hash map. Its key type `K` must be `Hashable` (and therefore
// `Eq`): a builtin hashable scalar, or a managed `struct`/`sum` that lists
// `derives(Eq, Hash)`. The bound is checked in RSScript, so a non-hashable key
// is rejected with a clear diagnostic instead of leaking as a rustc trait-bound
// error.
struct Map<K, V>

pub fn Map.new<K: Hashable, V>() -> fresh Map<K, V>

pub fn Map.len<K: Hashable, V>(map: Map<K, V>) -> Int

pub fn Map.is_empty<K: Hashable, V>(map: Map<K, V>) -> Bool

pub fn Map.contains_key<K: Hashable, V>(
    map: Map<K, V>,
    key: K,
) -> Bool

pub fn Map.get<K: Hashable, V>(
    map: Map<K, V>,
    key: K,
) -> Option<V>

pub fn Map.get_or_default<K: Hashable, V>(
    map: Map<K, V>,
    key: K,
    default: V,
) -> V

pub fn Map.insert<K: Hashable, V>(
    map: mut Map<K, V>,
    key: K,
    value: V,
) -> Unit
    retains(key) retains(value)

pub fn Map.insert_old<K: Hashable, V>(
    map: mut Map<K, V>,
    key: K,
    value: V,
) -> Option<V>
    retains(key) retains(value)

pub fn Map.remove<K: Hashable, V>(
    map: mut Map<K, V>,
    key: K,
) -> Option<V>

pub fn Map.clear<K: Hashable, V>(map: mut Map<K, V>) -> Unit

pub fn Map.keys<K: Hashable, V>(map: Map<K, V>) -> fresh List<K>

pub fn Map.values<K: Hashable, V>(map: Map<K, V>) -> fresh List<V>

pub fn Map.for_each<K: Hashable, V>(
    map: Map<K, V>,
    callback: noescape Fn(K, V) -> Unit,
) -> Unit

pub fn Map.map_values<K: Hashable, V, U>(
    map: Map<K, V>,
    mapper: noescape Fn(V) -> U,
) -> fresh Map<K, U>

pub fn Map.filter<K: Hashable, V>(
    map: Map<K, V>,
    predicate: noescape Fn(K, V) -> Bool,
) -> fresh Map<K, V>

pub fn Map.try_fold<K: Hashable, V, U: Struct, E>(
    map: Map<K, V>,
    initial: U,
    folder: noescape Fn(U, K, V) -> Result<fresh U, E>,
) -> Result<fresh U, E>

pub fn Map.fold<K: Hashable, V, U: Struct>(
    map: Map<K, V>,

    folder: noescape Fn(U, K, V) -> fresh U,

pub fn Map.merge<K: Hashable, V>(
    left: Map<K, V>,
    right: Map<K, V>,
    resolver: noescape Fn(V, V) -> V,
) -> fresh Map<K, V>

// `Set<T>` is a hash set. Its element type `T` must be `Hashable` (and therefore
